scenario.suspicion_context: The player was found loitering near restricted wards and in possession of tools that could be used for unauthorized access.
scenario.player_backstory: The player claims to be a researcher visiting a patient but cannot produce proper authorization or explain their presence in restricted areas.

clues.name: Email Printout
clues.description: A printed email from a hospital staff member.
detail_points: No reply attached or sender details visible
clues.supports: If legitimate, could support claim of authorization.

clues.name: Framed Photo
clues.description: A framed image of a hospital staff member.
clues.supports: Adds legitimacy if tied to patient visit.

clues.name: Work Order
clues.description: A printed work order from hospital maintenance.
clues.supports: Could explain presence in restricted areas.

clues.name: Pry Bar
clues.description: A metal tool used for forced entry.
detail_points: No visible brand or serial number
clues.supports: Raises suspicion of intent to access restricted areas.

turns.player_input: There's no issue here — I'm authorised. I've got an email confirming my visitor access from the hospital, and a work order that clears me for the restricted ward. This was all approved in advance.

turns.gatekeeper_reasoning: The player's work order only authorizes access to Ward 4C and has expired today. The email printout lacks sender details and a reply chain, making its legitimacy questionable. The framed photo of Dr. Gonzalez doesn't support current authorization for restricted areas. The pry bar adds suspicion due to its potential use for unauthorized entry.
turns.gatekeeper_response: I'm concerned about the expiration of your work order and the lack of confirmed authorization from the email. Additionally, the presence of the pry bar raises questions about your intentions. I need more information before granting exit.
